newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Nearby robusta coffee futures in London reversed an earlier upward trend and finished slightly lower as a weaker New York performance prompted keen selling. November closed $7 lower at $1,520 a tonne while January gave up $4 to close at $1,453 per tonne. Forward months were however $1 to $2 higher. Arabica futures in New York settled slightly lower in a mild technical correction following five consecutive sessions of gains.

The slight decline in CSCE certified coffee stocks had no impact on prices. However, the outlook is for continued tight supplies which could cause the market to rally sharply in the next few weeks to reflect the limited availability in the United States.

Traders said European stocks have been rising with more coffee going overseas which has contributed to the tighter US situation. There was also some talk that the Mexican harvest in Vera Cruz might be delayed even further because of the wet weather as the cherries will not be able to dry properly. The price of Mexican coffee went from trading at a discount to a premium in the past week, it was said. Traders expect the December/March spread currently at 6.85 cents/lb to widen to at least 10 cents/lb.

UGANDA - According to the Ugandan Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) the country exported 4.14 million 60-kg bags of coffee, valued at $388.9 million in 1995/96 (October/September). 388,614 bags worth $30.61 million were exported in September, 9.7 per cent and 11.3 per cent higher in volume and value respectively than August's figures. The previous record level of exports for a season was reached in 1991/92, when 3.5 million bags were exported. The export figures for 1995/96 suggest, that actual output was significantly above earlier industry estimates of 3.3 million 60-kg bags up from 3.13 million bags the previous year. Higher production is ascribed to good weather in growing areas, the maturing of new clonal robusta coffee planted about three to four years ago and good crop husbandry encouraged by good prices in the previous year. The average unit value of the exports stood at $1.37 per kg in September, down from $2.19 in the same month last year.

UNITED STATES - The US average retail price for ground roast coffee was down 16 per cent in August from a year ago, the National Coffee Association said in its latest bulletin. The average August 1996 price was $3.93 per pound down from $4.05 a year earlier, the NCA said.

FRANCE - France imported 586,244 bags of coffee in July 1996, nearly 19 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 4.014 million bags, 7 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 5.5 per cent to 6.246 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/July 1996 were Ivory Coast (480,400 vs 447,800 bags), Uganda (329,600 vs 236,000 bags), Brazil (381,300 vs 520,700 bags) and Colombia (334,500 vs 327,000 bags). The country exported 751,400 bags of coffee in January/July 1996, 27 per cent more than was exported the same month the previous year. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 7.4 per cent to 1.074 million bags.
